name: Articulated bus
description: A bus with two rigid sections joined by a pivoting articulation, allowing the vehicle to be much longer (typically 18 m, vs. 12 m for a standard bus) while still negotiating ordinary urban turning circles. The first articulated bus appeared in Milan, Italy, in 1937; in 1938 Twin Coach built one for the city of Baltimore (a 47-foot, four-axle vehicle articulated only in the vertical plane to handle steep grades). Articulated buses became central to the Bus Rapid Transit model from the 1970s onward — a single articulated vehicle carries 120–160 passengers, and the double-articulated 'biarticulated' designs used in Curitiba and elsewhere carry up to 270.
